title: Practise a Technical Interview with AI
summary: Run a structured mock interview that reveals gaps instead of rewarding memorised wording.
prerequisites: At least one completed technical module and one project example.

sections.heading: Choose a narrow practice goal
body: A useful mock interview has a scope. “Ask me Salesforce questions” can produce a random mixture of definitions, advanced features and outdated assumptions. Choose a level, two topics and a time limit. For example, a Junior session could cover objects, relationships and simple Apex tests. A Middle session could cover a callout failure and LWC state. A Senior session could examine access changes during an integration redesign.

Tell the assistant which parts of the Northstar project you have completed. Ask it to question your decisions rather than inventing employment history for you. It should ask one question at a time, wait for your answer and use a follow-up when your explanation is vague. Keep the first session short enough that you can review it properly.

callouts.text: The value of a mock interview is the next useful practice task, not a flattering score.

sections.heading: Set rules for evidence and feedback
body: An AI interviewer can be mistaken, especially about changing platform behaviour and product availability. Ask it to separate factual feedback from communication feedback. A factual correction should include a current official source that you can verify. “Your answer was difficult to follow” is communication feedback and needs an example from your response rather than a documentation link.

Use a small rubric: technical correctness, reasoning, evidence and clarity. Score each as missing, partial or clear. If you say “use asynchronous Apex,” the follow-up should ask which mechanism, why it fits and what happens on failure. This tests understanding more effectively than giving full credit for a keyword.

codeBlocks.caption: Reusable working prompt or template
codeBlocks.code:
Act as a practice interviewer for [level] Salesforce development.
Topics: [two topics]. Project context: [what I actually built].
Ask one question at a time and wait for my answer.
Use a follow-up when I make an unsupported claim. Do not reveal the answer first.
After five questions, review correctness, reasoning, evidence and clarity.
Quote the specific part of my answer behind each observation.
For platform corrections, provide an official source and identify version assumptions.
Mark uncertainty. Do not invent a hiring result or guarantee my level.

sections.heading: Answer with a decision and a reason
body: Use a simple response structure: state the relevant fact or decision, explain why, give an example and mention an important boundary. For “Why use a lookup here?”, you might explain that the test-drive record has its own ownership and sharing requirements, show the model and discuss what a master-detail alternative would change. Do not force every answer into a long speech; the structure is a guide, not a script.

When you do not know, identify the missing fact and explain how you would verify it. “I would check the current limit and the expected volume before choosing the batch size” is useful if you can also explain the design issue. Avoid using uncertainty as a way to say nothing: give the part you understand, then mark the boundary.

callouts.text: Record your answer before reading the model explanation. Otherwise you may mistake recognition for recall.

sections.heading: Review the transcript and retry one problem
body: After the session, choose two weak answers and verify the assistant’s feedback against official documentation or your own reproducible test. Keep a table with question, your original answer, confirmed issue and next exercise. Reject a correction if its evidence does not support it; the assistant is a practice partner, not the final authority.

Repeat a related question with a changed condition. If the first question used a single record, ask about a batch. If it assumed private sharing, ask what changes with another access path. You should be able to explain the changed reasoning. Repeating the exact wording until it sounds fluent is not enough to establish understanding.

callouts.text: You can explain one correction, cite or demonstrate why it is correct and answer a variation without reading your notes.

exercise.title: Apply this to your own search
exercise.brief: Run a five-question mock interview and turn it into a small practice plan.
steps: Choose a level and two topics.
Use the prompt and answer before viewing feedback.
Rewrite the weakest answer in your own words.
Answer a variation that changes an important condition.
acceptance: The session contains follow-up questions, not only definitions.
Corrections are supported or explicitly marked uncertain.
The final plan names a concrete exercise rather than “study more.”

knowledgeCheck.question: Is an AI interview score a reliable hiring prediction?
knowledgeCheck.answer: No. It is practice feedback and can be inconsistent or wrong.

knowledgeCheck.question: How can you check whether you understand a corrected answer?
knowledgeCheck.answer: Explain the mechanism and solve a variation with changed conditions.

knowledgeCheck.question: What should you do with an unsupported correction?
knowledgeCheck.answer: Verify it using official documentation or a suitable experiment before accepting it.

illustration.prompt: Create one landscape 16:9 lesson-cover illustration for SAM Salesforce Developer Studio. Restrained professional editorial illustration, flat geometric drawn forms with fine navy linework and a subtle paper texture. Warm ivory #F7F4EE, navy #12253C, muted cobalt #3867E8, restrained teal #138A86 and sage. One clear central scene, generous empty margins, at most three main visual groups. Calm adult learning design. Any people are clearly drawn stylized figures, never realistic photos. NO text, letters, numerals, logos, watermarks, Salesforce mascots, decorative clutter or glossy 3D. Exact topic: Practise an Interview. Subject: two simply drawn people discussing one technical diagram with a reflective note card.
